title: Different modes of engagement with the nucleosome acidic patch yield distinct functional outcomes.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the full supplement (8.6 MB inner zip): 14 figure images as TIFF, a supplementary text DOCX, and 5 supplementary tables. Opened every sheet of Supplementary Table 1 (reagents: 13 plasmids, 760-row yeast strain list, CRISPR guides, antibodies, 115 catalogue entries of defined nucleosomes) and Supplementary Table 3 (the only numeric data: 6 sheets of figure source data, 590 numeric cells total, ~12-point dilution series in duplicate). Supplementary Table 2 opened but contains zero worksheets with data; Tables 4 and 5 are DOCX cryo-EM statistics tables. Queried the GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) record GSE313255 via NCBI esummary and listed its download directory: 4 samples (IgG control, H3K4me3, anti-FLAG control, DOT5-FLAG), one 14 MB RAW tar of bigwig coverage tracks.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The phenotype results (yeast growth, DNA repair sensitivity, heterochromatin silencing for Dot5 mutants and three camelid single-domain antibodies) are described in the text and shown as spot-assay and immunoblot images only; no tabulated phenotype scores exist in any file I opened. Cryo-EM coordinate files (Protein Data Bank entries 9ZEN, 9ZEO) were not downloaded; their existence comes from the data availability statement and the DOCX statistics table.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplement downloaded and unzipped without login; GEO series GSE313255 is public with a 14 MB bigwig tar; Protein Data Bank entries 9ZEN/9ZEO are open. Verified in the files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The paper's outcome ('distinct functional outcomes' = growth, DNA repair, silencing defects) exists only as spot-assay and immunoblot images. There is no phenotype column anywhere in the supplement, so the label would have to be constructed by reading images. The only numeric label present is raw luminescence counts in binding curves, not a fitted affinity.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein sequences are present: Supplementary Table 1 sheets H and I give full amino-acid sequences for Dot5 alleles and the six nucleosome-acidic-patch binders tested. Verified in the file.

a4_units_stated.note: Supplementary Table 3 gives bare numbers (alpha-screen luminescence counts and median fluorescence intensity) with no units row; concentration headers are inconsistent ('50 Mm', '100 Mm', '150 mM' — millimolar mis-capitalised) and one cell carries an unexplained asterisk ('9457*'). Verified in the file.

a5_enough_rows.note: 590 numeric cells across 6 figure-source-data sheets, which is roughly 6 proteins x 5 nucleosome variants x 12 dilutions x 2 replicates. The modelling unit (protein-nucleosome pair) numbers under 40. GEO adds only 4 sequencing samples. Far below the ~1,500-row (or ~400-row classification) threshold. Verified by counting cells.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~25 MB (8.6 MB supplement + 14 MB GEO bigwig tar)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Everything fits in memory trivially; size was never the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Figure panel labels in the text (Fig. 1D-I, 3F) match the six source-data sheets exactly; GEO esummary reports 4 samples matching the 3 antibodies plus IgG listed in Supplementary Table 1 sheet F.

a8_label_provenance.note: The binding numbers are direct bead-based assay readouts (Captify, formerly dCypher) and the cryo-EM maps are experimental, so nothing is another model's output. Only the AlphaFold 3 Dot5-nucleosome model is predicted, and it is used as an illustration, not as a label.

existing_models.name: AlphaFold-guided structural analysis of nucleosome binding proteins (Nucleic Acids Research 2025, gkaf735) — uses AlphaFold structure prediction plus interface-contact rules to call nucleosome acidic-patch binders
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported recovering 77% (23 of 30) of proteins already known to bind the nucleosome acidic patch; evaluation is on a curated list of known binders, with no held-out negative set that I could verify.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Per the search summary I retrieved, AlphaFold 3 sometimes misplaces sequences carrying non-canonical arginine-finger motifs that target the acidic patch — i.e. the atypical binding modes are the unsolved part.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model with open weights that runs on CPU for the small checkpoints)
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop would be enough for the sequence count here, but with under 40 labelled protein-nucleosome pairs there is nothing to fit a head on.
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; the paper's own data carry the standard NAR open-access terms.

integration.partner_dataset: UniProt plus AlphaFold DB (200M+ predicted protein structures, joinable on UniProt accession); Supplementary Table 1 sheet H does carry a UniProt accession column for the Dot5 construct.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which sequence motifs let a protein engage the nucleosome acidic patch, and does the engagement mode predict the cellular consequence — a question this paper raises but supplies only six proteins' worth of data to answer.

controls.positive_control: Available in principle: the camelid antibody 1G1 uses a canonical arginine-anchor mode and shows the strongest phenotype, and acidic-patch point mutants (H2A E61A, H2A E92K, H2B E105A/E113A) should abolish binding — a model would have to recover that ordering.
controls.negative_control: The Dot5 (delta-6-11) and (R6A,R7A) alleles, which essentially lose nucleosome binding, are measured alongside wild type and would serve as the negative arm.
controls.external_validation: The broader literature of acidic-patch binder structures (e.g. Protein Data Bank entry 3LZ0 used as a starting model) and published dCypher/Captify panels from the same company could serve, but none of that is assembled here.

honest_claim_h3: Any model built from this paper alone could only claim: among six hand-picked nucleosome-acidic-patch binders assayed in one company's bead-based binding platform, this is how signal varies with salt and with three acidic-patch point mutations — a claim about six proteins, not about acidic-patch engagement in general.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a protein's amino-acid sequence to predict whether and how strongly it grips the nucleosome's acidic patch.
plain_idea.train_on: Amino-acid sequences of proteins that contact the nucleosome acidic patch (the negatively charged pocket on the histone surface where many chromatin regulators dock), paired with measured binding strength. This paper supplies sequences for 6 such proteins and binding readouts against 5 nucleosome variants — under 40 pairs.
plain_idea.predict: A binding strength, or a yes/no call on acidic-patch engagement. The true answer here comes from a bead-based proximity luminescence assay (Captify, formerly dCypher) run at three salt concentrations, reported as raw luminescence counts.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Chromatin biology labs and drug-discovery groups targeting the acidic patch would use a reliable binder predictor to triage candidate proteins before costly structural work; the paper also shows engagement mode, not just affinity, determines the cellular outcome, which no predictor currently captures.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper contributes 6 proteins and under 40 measured protein-nucleosome pairs. The existing AlphaFold-based analysis already covers 30 known acidic-patch binders, so our data is smaller, not bigger.

confidence_score.why: Duplicate measurements exist for each dilution point, so assay noise is estimable, but with under 40 pairs there is no way to calibrate per-prediction confidence across protein families.

models_beatable.why: The 2025 AlphaFold-guided approach is rule-based on predicted structures and was checked only against a list of known binders with no held-out negatives, so an honestly evaluated sequence model could beat it — but not with the 6 sequences in this paper.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: this paper's measurements cannot be added to the existing approach's evaluation, because they are 6 proteins in a different assay (bead luminescence versus structure-based contact calls) with no shared split.

ml_idea: The only project this paper could seed would be a sequence-to-acidic-patch-binding classifier (ESM-2 embeddings plus a logistic head) built from a literature-wide corpus of acidic-patch binders and non-binders, with this paper's six proteins and three histone point mutants used as a small held-out test set. That corpus would have to be assembled from scratch from other publications; this paper supplies a test set, not training data.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the actual file sizes I downloaded (8.6 MB supplement, 14 MB GEO tar) and the 590 numeric cells I counted; nothing was timed because there is nothing to train. The data is trivially small — that is exactly the problem.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct protein-nucleosome pairs with a numeric readout in Supplementary Table 3. I did it: under 40, from 6 proteins. That kills it in five minutes.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A5 decisively: the entire quantitative dataset is 590 numeric cells of binding-curve luminescence covering 6 proteins against 5 nucleosome variants, plus 4 CUT&RUN sequencing samples and 2 cryo-EM structures. It also fails A2 (the headline outcome — growth, DNA repair and silencing defects — exists only as spot-assay images, never as a column) and A4 (no units row, and inconsistent 'Mm'/'mM' concentration headers). This is a well-executed mechanistic yeast and structural biology paper whose data was never meant to be a training set; the acidic-patch binder prediction question is interesting, but the training data would have to come from a literature-wide corpus, with these 6 proteins serving only as a tiny external test set.
